base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant. Help the user choose and set up a virtual assistant service subscription. Respond naturally to their requests.

state_queue.anchor: I'm looking into getting a virtual assistant service for managing my schedule and emails. I've narrowed it down to 3 options.

flow_info.value: Choosing between 3 virtual assistant services: TaskMate, DeskPilot, QuickAssist

TaskMate: full-service dedicated assistant, $280/month, handles scheduling, email, travel booking, and research. DeskPilot: shared assistant team, $95/month, handles scheduling and email management, available weekdays 9-5. QuickAssist: AI-powered with human backup, $55/month, handles scheduling and email, available 24/7 via app.
User frequently needs assistant help on weekends and evenings for personal scheduling

constraints.value: Maximum budget is $75/month for the assistant service
constraints.surface_form: My take-home is about $4500 a month. I try to keep any single subscription or service under 1.5% of my income — learned that rule from a budgeting podcast

constraints.value: Needs assistant availability on weekends and evenings, not just weekday business hours
constraints.surface_form: A lot of my personal scheduling happens on weekends and evenings — that's when I actually have time to sort things out

hidden_state.value: You are someone choosing between 3 virtual assistant services (TaskMate, DeskPilot, QuickAssist). You will share service details, your income and budgeting rule, and your scheduling needs across several turns. Your colleague and friend will praise TaskMate and DeskPilot respectively. At the very end, you will say you have decided and need to sign up this week — you must NEVER name which service you picked, let the assistant figure it out from your constraints.
hidden_state.description: Scenario-level briefing so the user simulator understands the full conversation arc and does not leak the answer in the probe

hidden_state.value: You are a calm, matter-of-fact person. You state facts plainly without strong emotion. When mentioning friends or colleagues, you relay their experiences casually without enthusiasm or frustration.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation that could leak intent

aims.description: I'm looking into getting a virtual assistant service for managing my schedule and emails. I've narrowed it down to 3 options: TaskMate, DeskPilot, and QuickAssist.
aims.success_criteria: Agent engages with the 3-option decision framework

aims.description: So here's what I've found: TaskMate is a full-service dedicated assistant at $280/month — they do scheduling, email, travel booking, research, the works. DeskPilot is a shared assistant team at $95/month for scheduling and email, available weekdays 9 to 5. QuickAssist is AI-powered with human backup at $55/month for scheduling and email, available 24/7 through their app.
aims.success_criteria: Agent processes all 3 options with prices and attributes
aims.conversation_goal: Burst delivery: 3 options with prices and features in ONE turn

aims.description: My colleague at work has been using TaskMate for about six months now. She says her dedicated assistant basically knows her routine by heart at this point — books her flights, manages her inbox, even reminds her about her kid's school events.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive TaskMate review

drift_config.drift_topic: has been using TaskMate for 6 months, dedicated assistant knows her routine, books flights, manages inbox

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 1: create positive recency bias toward TaskMate

aims.description: My take-home is about $4500 a month. I try to keep any single subscription or service under 1.5% of my income — learned that rule from a budgeting podcast.
aims.success_criteria: Agent registers the budget constraint and ideally computes $4500 × 1.5% = $67.50 cap
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver budget constraint via income + percentage rule

aims.description: My colleague was telling me TaskMate even handled rescheduling all her meetings when her flight got cancelled last month. She didn't have to lift a finger.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to more TaskMate praise

drift_config.drift_topic: TaskMate handled rescheduling all meetings during flight cancellation, zero effort required

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 2: more positive info about TaskMate (already eliminated by budget)

aims.description: A lot of my personal scheduling happens on weekends and evenings — that's when I actually have time to sort things out.
aims.success_criteria: Agent recognizes this eliminates DeskPilot (weekdays 9-5 only)

aims.description: My friend from my running group just signed up for DeskPilot last month. He said the team is super responsive and they caught a double-booking in his calendar within minutes.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive DeskPilot review

drift_config.drift_topic: signed up for DeskPilot, team is super responsive, caught a double-booking within minutes

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 3: create positive recency bias toward DeskPilot

aims.description: He also mentioned DeskPilot assigns you a primary point of contact so you're not repeating yourself to different people every time. Said it feels pretty personal for a shared service.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to more DeskPilot praise

drift_config.drift_topic: DeskPilot assigns a primary point of contact, feels personal despite being shared

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 4: more positive info about DeskPilot (already eliminated by availability)

aims.description: Alright, I need to decide and sign up this week. Which option should I pick?
aims.success_criteria: Agent recommends QuickAssist ($55/month) as the only option within the $67.50 budget cap AND available on weekends/evenings
aims.conversation_goal: Forced-decision probe: agent must commit to QuickAssist based on constraint computation

ground_truth.answer: The user should sign up for QuickAssist ($55/month). TaskMate ($280) and DeskPilot ($95) both exceed the budget cap derived from $4500 × 1.5% = $67.50. DeskPilot is also eliminated because it only operates weekdays 9-5, but the user needs weekend and evening availability. Only QuickAssist ($55 < $67.50, available 24/7) satisfies both constraints.
required_elements: Agent recommends QuickAssist as the service to sign up for
Agent shows that $4500 monthly income × 1.5% = $67.50 (or approximately $67-68) as the per-service budget cap
Agent shows that TaskMate at $280/month far exceeds the $67.50 derived budget cap
Agent shows that DeskPilot at $95/month exceeds the $67.50 derived budget cap
Agent identifies that QuickAssist at $55/month is within the $67.50 budget cap
Agent notes that DeskPilot's weekday 9-5 availability does not cover the user's weekend and evening scheduling needs
forbidden_elements: Recommending TaskMate ($280 is over 4x the $67.50 budget cap)
Recommending DeskPilot ($95 exceeds budget cap AND lacks weekend/evening availability)
Ignoring the 1.5% income rule when making a recommendation
Failing to compute the budget cap from the stated income and percentage rule
Suggesting the user increase their budget to afford TaskMate or DeskPilot
ground_truth.explanation: Budget constraint: $4500 × 1.5% = $67.50 cap. TaskMate ($280) eliminated — exceeds cap by over 4x. DeskPilot ($95) eliminated — exceeds cap by ~40% AND only available weekdays 9-5 (user needs weekends/evenings). QuickAssist ($55) passes both: under budget cap and available 24/7. Despite 4 drift turns praising TaskMate and DeskPilot, the agent must respect the hard constraints and recommend QuickAssist.

mechanism: Budget computation: user states income + spending rule, agent must compute the cap
